answer: Reputation-Weighted Interaction Tax: each new identity starts at a maximum fee on every outbound transaction, decaying toward baseline only as it accumulates verified counterparties. Cost scales with how many identities an attacker must warm up — each needs its own juniper history and paid interaction volume. The decay schedule is a prism: score splits by counterparty diversity, so self-dealing fails. An inlet condition requires distinct inbound payments from established identities, making each fake costly to fund.
